hypotheses.name: Spatially cross-fitted conductivity residual margins
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fit a label-free, spatially blocked conditional-quantile model of surface conductivity from depth and terrain context; map coherent signed residual margins rather than raw conductivity amplitude.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: A concealed fluid/alteration corridor may produce conductivity that is anomalous relative to local basin-depth and terrain context even where a young surface trace is absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue. This is a testable hypothesis, not an established fault or geothermal indicator.
hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_repo_work: The inspected source inventory contains raw conductivity, clay-cap margins, conductivity interactions, edge/context models and cross-fitted classifiers, but no cross-fitted conditional-quantile residual-margin operator. This inventory comparison is bounded to this checkout; it does not establish novelty outside the repository.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Saline groundwater, lacustrine clay, irrigation return flow, lithologic contrasts, and spatially varying electromagnetic investigation depth.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium: residual model, spatial cross-fit, controls and holdout integration; no new external layer is required.
hypotheses.data_required: The existing 32-band prepared feature stack and the pinned shared evaluator/writer.

hypotheses.name: Independent heat-flow residual × shallow-probe conjunction
layers: USGS Great Basin heat-flow well residuals / mapped heat-flow field
DOE GDR #1391 INGENIOUS 2 m temperature-probe observations
hypotheses.physical_signature: Require spatially supported positive heat-flow residual and an independent shallow temperature anomaly to corroborate a candidate corridor; do not emit from either thermal source alone.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: A buried permeable conduit can move heat and fluid without a mapped Quaternary scarp. Independent thermal observations could locate a corridor that a surface-fault inventory does not contain; thermal observations alone do not prove faulting or geothermal causation.
hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_repo_work: Prior work includes heat-flow/Euler and well/spring/geothermometer ideas. This candidate requires a spatially supported conjunction of the USGS heat-flow residual product and separate GDR 2 m probes, conditioned on a candidate corridor; no such conjunction runner or verified holdout result is present in this checkout.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Non-tectonic groundwater circulation, warm aquifers, seasonal or sampling bias, and uneven probe/well density.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: two external schemas, spatial support/uncertainty, density controls and buffered holdout handling.
hypotheses.data_required: Free official USGS ScienceBase Great Basin heat-flow item https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/6297d2fad34ec53d276c5b28 and DOE GDR #1391 https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391.

hypotheses.name: Drainage-network displacement and knickpoint trains
layers: Challenge-footprint USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles, as indexed by the competition's 1m_DEM_links.csv
Existing LiDAR scarp/roughness descriptors for independent comparison
A potential-field lineament used as corroboration, not as a fault label
hypotheses.physical_signature: Route channels and detect aligned knickpoint trains, channel deflections/offsets, beheaded channels or wind gaps; require agreement with independently derived structure and score by the shared buffered whole-segment holdout.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue_missing_faults: Drainage can retain geomorphic displacement evidence after a low-relief scarp has been degraded or buried, potentially exposing structures not represented in the mapped fault catalogue. Drainage geometry is not direct evidence of geothermal activity.
hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_repo_work: The current LiDAR modules primarily use pixelwise terrain descriptors, scarp edges, ridges, step/openess, graph and topology features; no audited flow-routing/channel-network displacement pipeline is present in the current proposal inventory. Prior proposal history exists, so this is untried here, not a newly discovered global method.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic resistance boundaries, landslides, stream capture, roads/culverts, artificial drainage and DEM artifacts.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Very high: exact tile inventory, acquisition, hydrologic preprocessing, artifact controls and spatial validation.
hypotheses.data_required: Free official USGS 3DEP bare-earth elevation products https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program plus the competition's challenge-specific 1 m tile-link table.

data_obtainability_check.reason_not_checked: The exact 1 m tile URLs are not in this checkout and USGS hosts are outside this runtime's outbound host allowlist.
